task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm hoping you can help me out. For the past few hours I haven't been able to send picture messages — you know, MMS — from my messaging app. Regular texts seem to go through fine, but anything with a photo just sits there and fails. It's been pretty frustrating.

turns.thought:
I’d be happy to help you get picture messaging (MMS) working again. To get started, I need to pull up your account and identify the line that’s having trouble.

Could you please provide either:
- the **phone number** of the line you're having the issue with, or
- your **full name** and **date of birth** (for verification)?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure thing — my name is John Smith, and the phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else from me.

turns.thought:
I've located your account, John. Here's what I can see:

- **Line:** 555-123-2002 (L1002) — status **Active**
- **Plan:** Premium Plan, 15 GB limit — you've used **8.7 GB**, so you're well within your data allowance
- **Bills:** Your January bill is paid; the February bill ($150.00) is issued but not due until 2025-02-19, so nothing is overdue

Since your line is active, data is available, and there's no billing issue, this looks like a device-side MMS configuration problem rather than an account problem. Let's troubleshoot the phone itself.

Please start by checking two things on your phone and tell me what you see:

1. **Your status bar** (top of the screen) — is there a signal strength indicator? Do you see a network type like 5G, LTE/4G, or 3G? Is mobile data enabled?
2. **Your APN settings** — specifically, is there an **MMSC URL** listed? This is the setting most commonly responsible for picture messages failing while regular texts work fine.

Once you tell me what those show, I'll walk you through the specific fix.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at both of those for you.

turns.thought:
Good catch — and yes, I think we've found it. Regular texts (SMS) can sometimes still appear to go through over Wi-Fi or get queued up, but **picture messages (MMS) require an active cellular data connection. Airplane Mode disables all wireless radios, including cellular, which will cause MMS to fail every time** while some other functions may still seem to work.

The good news is your APN settings look correct — the MMSC URL (`http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc`) is properly set, so we don't need to touch those.

Here's what I'd like you to do:

**Step 1 — Turn Airplane Mode OFF**
- If you can run `toggle_airplane_mode()` on your device, use that to switch it off.
- Otherwise: swipe down from the top of your screen to open Quick Settings, and tap the **Airplane Mode** tile so it's no longer highlighted. (You can also go to **Settings > Network & Internet** and toggle Airplane Mode off there.)

**Step 2 — Check your status bar again**
Once it's off, wait about 10–15 seconds for the phone to reconnect, then check the status bar and confirm:
- The airplane icon is **gone**
- You now see **signal bars** (📶) and a network type like 5G/LTE/4G
- Mobile data shows as **enabled**

**Step 3 — Test picture messaging**
Try sending a photo message again. If you can run `can_send_mms()` on your device, that will confirm whether it's working.

**Step 4 (if still failing)**
If it works — great, that was the whole issue. If picture messages still fail now that Airplane Mode is off, please tell me:
- What your status bar shows now (signal strength + network type)
- Whether mobile data is enabled
- Whether Wi-Fi is connected

Then I can dig into the next most likely causes — mobile data being switched off, Wi-Fi Calling interference, or the messaging app missing its storage/SMS permissions.

Go ahead and try that, and let me know what you see afterward.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn Airplane Mode off first.

turns.thought:
Good news — turning off Airplane Mode definitely helped restore your cellular connection (full bars on 5G with data enabled means your line and account are fine on our end). So we've cleared the first hurdle. Since MMS is still failing, we need to work through the remaining common causes.

Two things to check next — these are the most likely culprits now that your connection is solid:

**Step 1 — Check Wi-Fi Calling**
Wi-Fi Calling can sometimes conflict with MMS, especially when the carrier doesn't route MMS over Wi-Fi. On your device, run `check_wifi_calling_status()`.
- If it reports **Wi-Fi Calling is ON**, run `toggle_wifi_calling()` to turn it OFF, then try sending a picture message again.

**Step 2 — Check the messaging app's permissions**
The messaging app needs **storage** access (to read your photos) and **SMS** access (to send the message). Missing permissions is a very common reason MMS fails while plain texts work.
- Run `check_app_permissions(app_name="messaging")`.
- If **storage** isn't granted, run `grant_app_permission(app_name="messaging", permission="storage")`.
- If **sms** isn't granted, run `grant_app_permission(app_name="messaging", permission="sms")`.
- Then try sending a photo again.

A couple of other quick things worth confirming while you're in there:
- `run_speed_test()` — just to confirm data is actually flowing (MMS only needs a minimal connection, but this rules out a silent data drop).
- `check_network_status()` — confirm the reported network type is 5G/4G and not 2G (2G generally can't carry MMS).

Please try Step 1 and Step 2 and let me know what each one reports — and whether the picture message goes through afterward. If Wi-Fi Calling and the app permissions both check out and it's still failing, I'll take it from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take these one at a time so I don't mess anything up. Starting with the Wi-Fi Calling check.

turns.thought:
Yes, please do — that's exactly the right next step, and it'll help us narrow things down quickly.

Since the messaging app permissions check out (sms, storage, and phone all granted — good), let's confirm the data path is actually working end to end. Please run these on your device and let me know what each reports:

1. **`run_speed_test()`** — This tells us whether data is genuinely flowing. MMS only needs a very minimal connection, so even a "poor" result should technically be enough for a small photo, but a "no connection" result would point to a data-side problem we still need to fix.

2. **`check_network_status()`** — Confirm the network type it reports. It should show 5G or 4G/LTE. If it shows **2G**, that's a problem, because 2G generally can't carry MMS, and we'd fix it by setting the network mode preference to `4g_5g_preferred`.

3. **`check_wifi_calling_status()`** — We didn't get to this one earlier. Wi-Fi Calling being ON is a known cause of MMS failures on some configurations. If it's on, I'll have you turn it off.

4. **`check_data_restriction_status()`** — Check whether Data Saver mode is on. Data Saver restricts background data and can block the messaging app from completing an MMS send even when your main data connection is fine.

Go ahead and run those four when you get a moment and paste back whatever they show. With your results in hand we should be able to pinpoint this — and if it turns out to be something on the account or provisioning side rather than the device, I'll take it from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me run those checks for you.

turns.thought:
That's the missing piece — and your instinct is exactly right. Here's what's going on:

**Your line is actually fine on our end.** I checked your line (555-123-2002) and it is **already roaming-enabled**, and you've only used 8.7 GB of your 15 GB allowance — so there's plenty of data available and **you don't need to add data or change your plan**.

The problem is purely on the phone: **the Data Roaming switch on the device is turned off.** That explains the contradiction you spotted perfectly. Your phone has a strong 5G signal (it's connected to a partner network here in France), and mobile data is enabled in general — but because the roaming toggle is off, the phone refuses to actually pass data over a non-home network. So you show "connected with excellent signal" while every real data request, including MMS, fails with no connection. That's also why speed test failed while SMS still worked.

Let's fix it:

**Step 1 — Turn Data Roaming ON**
- Run `toggle_roaming()` on your device to switch Data Roaming ON.
- Or manually: **Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network** (or *SIMs* / *Cellular*), and turn **Data Roaming** (sometimes called "Roaming" or "Data while roaming") **ON**.

**Step 2 — Re-check the data path**
- Run `run_speed_test()` again — it should now return an actual speed result instead of "No Connection."

**Step 3 — Test picture messaging**
- Try sending a photo message again, or run `can_send_mms()` to confirm.

One note on costs: since you're abroad, data used while roaming works differently than domestic usage — I'd recommend checking your plan's international roaming terms so you know what to expect on your next bill. I don't want to quote you specifics I can't confirm from your account details.

Also, if for any reason Data Roaming was already managed on the account side and you'd rather not enable it on the device, an alternative short-term workaround would be connecting to Wi-Fi and using an internet-based messaging app instead of MMS — but let's try the roaming toggle first since that should get your normal picture messaging working.

Go ahead and try that and let me know what the speed test and MMS check report afterward. If it works, we're done. If it still fails with roaming on, I'll escalate further on the provisioning side.
turns.execution_output: User: That makes sense — let me turn data roaming on.

turns.thought:
You've got it exactly right — that's a perfect summary of the root cause:

- Your **line was roaming-enabled and healthy** on our end
- You had **plenty of data** left (8.7 GB of 15 GB)
- No plan change, no extra data purchase needed
- The only problem was the **Data Roaming switch being OFF on your phone**, which blocked all data — and therefore MMS — while you're on a partner network in France

Glad the speed test came back at 275 Mbps and picture messaging is working again.

On your last question: the Data Roaming setting governs whether your phone will use data on networks **outside your home network**, so once you're back in the US it isn't coming into play for your normal usage. I'll leave the choice to you rather than tell you how to set your own device — **if you'd like me to switch it back off for you once you're home, just say the word and I can do that** for line 555-123-2002.

One thing worth doing before your next trip: switching Data Roaming ON ahead of time would have prevented this. And it's a good idea to review your plan's international roaming terms beforehand so you know what to expect on your bill — I can't confirm those specifics from what I have in front of me.

Safe travels, and enjoy the rest of your time in France! Anything else I can help with?
